turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (NURSE): Morning, Mrs Botha. I'll take your blood pressure before Doctor Naidoo sees you.
[SEG0002] person_2 (PATIENT): Ag, is that necessary? I'm only here because of that recall letter.
[SEG0003] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Morning. Piet, her husband. We left the bakkie on a yellow line, so ja, the quicker the better.
[SEG0004] person_1 (NURSE): Shame, we'll be quick. Arm nice and loose, please.
[SEG0005] person_2 (PATIENT): The chemist did it last week and it was fine. I don't see why we do it again.
[SEG0006] person_1 (NURSE): We still need today's number for the file. Just hold still a moment.
[SEG0007] person_1 (NURSE): Okay. One hundred and forty-eight over ninety-two.
[SEG0008] person_2 (PATIENT): Hmph. If you say so. Whole fuss over nothing, hey.
[SEG0009] person_4 (DOCTOR): Howzit Elaine, Piet. Come sit. How have you been keeping, really?
[SEG0010] person_2 (PATIENT): Fine. Completely fine. I don't even know what we're supposed to talk about.
[SEG0011] person_4 (DOCTOR): It's your routine blood pressure and cholesterol review. In your own words, how's things at home?
[SEG0012] person_2 (PATIENT): Lekker. Garden, rugby on the telly. A bit tired in the afternoons, but that's just being sixty-seven. Nothing medical.
[SEG0013] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): She nods off in the chair after lunch. Most days, not just now and then.
[SEG0014] person_2 (PATIENT): Ag Piet, everyone does that. It's not a thing.
[SEG0015] person_4 (DOCTOR): When you walk up to the shop, any chest pain, or feeling short of breath?
[SEG0016] person_2 (PATIENT): No. No chest pain, and I'm not short of breath. I walk fine.
[SEG0017] person_4 (DOCTOR): And headaches, or any dizziness?
[SEG0018] person_2 (PATIENT): No headaches. Not dizzy.
[SEG0019] person_2 (PATIENT): Well, actually, a small one now and then, behind the eyes. I just ignore it.
[SEG0020] person_4 (DOCTOR): Alright. Talk me through the tablets you're actually taking at home.
[SEG0021] person_2 (PATIENT): Just the blood pressure one. Amlodipine. Every other day. Every day is overkill, my pressure's fine.
[SEG0022] person_1 (NURSE): Sorry, Doctor. The script on the file says amlodipine ten milligrams, once a day.
[SEG0023] person_2 (PATIENT): No man. It's the five. Little white tablet. Ten would knock me flat.
[SEG0024] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): I looked in the cupboard this morning. The box says five milligrams.
[SEG0025] person_4 (DOCTOR): So the file and the box don't agree, and that's alright, we'll sort the strength when we see the box. You're taking it every second day, not every day?
[SEG0026] person_2 (PATIENT): Ja. Every other day. Works for me.
[SEG0027] person_4 (DOCTOR): What about the cholesterol tablet, the atorvastatin?
[SEG0028] person_2 (PATIENT): Oh, I stopped that. Read something online, memory and muscles and all that, so I left it.
[SEG0029] person_4 (DOCTOR): Were the muscles actually sore, or was it just what you read?
[SEG0030] person_2 (PATIENT): Never sore. I just stopped. In March, I think. Or maybe April. I can't pin the month.
[SEG0031] person_4 (DOCTOR): Do you remember the strength of it?
[SEG0032] person_2 (PATIENT): Twenty milligrams, at night. Not that I'm taking it anymore.
[SEG0033] person_4 (DOCTOR): Was anything else written up that you never started? Aspirin, sometimes, after a hospital visit.
[SEG0034] person_2 (PATIENT): Ja, they mentioned aspirin at the hospital. I never took it. Not even once. Seemed pointless.
[SEG0035] person_4 (DOCTOR): Okay, so that never got going. Any sugar tablets for yourself?
[SEG0036] person_2 (PATIENT): No, that's Piet's. He takes metformin for his diabetes. They said my sugar is normal.
[SEG0037] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Five hundred milligrams, twice a day, with food. That's mine.
[SEG0038] person_4 (DOCTOR): We'll keep his pills off your list entirely. Any allergies to medicines?
[SEG0039] person_2 (PATIENT): No. Nothing I'm allergic to.
[SEG0040] person_4 (DOCTOR): Heart attacks or strokes in the family?
[SEG0041] person_2 (PATIENT): My dad had a heart attack. He was in his seventies already. Mom was fine, she just got old.
[SEG0042] person_4 (DOCTOR): Do you smoke at all?
[SEG0043] person_2 (PATIENT): Never. Can't stand the smell.
[SEG0044] person_4 (DOCTOR): And alcohol?
[SEG0045] person_2 (PATIENT): A glass of wine if there's a braai. I'm not a drinker.
[SEG0046] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Ja, one glass at the Saturday braai. Oh, and that robot by the chemist was out this morning, traffic was mad.
[SEG0047] person_2 (PATIENT): We sat there forever. Anyway. Not important.
[SEG0048] person_4 (DOCTOR): Eish, that corner. Let me listen to your chest. Nice deep breath.
[SEG0049] person_4 (DOCTOR): Chest is clear, heart sounds are normal, and the pulse is regular at seventy-two. Ankles aren't swollen.
[SEG0050] person_2 (PATIENT): See? Nothing wrong with me.

[SEG0051] person_4 (DOCTOR): You look well, and I'm not going to scold you for stopping the statin. My thought is the pressure is still a bit high today, and off the atorvastatin the cholesterol may have crept up. Working idea, not a verdict.
[SEG0052] person_2 (PATIENT): I had blood tests already. Recently. Well, I think I did.
[SEG0053] person_4 (DOCTOR): Can you place when that was?
[SEG0054] person_2 (PATIENT): Um. Last year, or early this year. I honestly can't say.

[SEG0055] person_4 (DOCTOR): Then we'll repeat them. A lipid panel for the cholesterol, kidney function because you're on a blood pressure tablet, and a fasting glucose so we know the sugar story is yours. Tomorrow morning at the lab, before any coffee.
[SEG0056] person_1 (NURSE): I'll print the lab form for you. Fasting, tomorrow morning.

[SEG0057] person_4 (DOCTOR): The statin we look at together in a month, when the results are back. If the cholesterol is up we can talk about a lower dose. If it's fine, it stays off. No pressure from me today.
[SEG0058] person_2 (PATIENT): A month is fine. I'm not promising I'll start it again, hey.
[SEG0059] person_4 (DOCTOR): That's fair. Please take the amlodipine every day till then, not every second day, and bring the box so we can see five or ten. See you in a month. Cheers.

features: disputed_numbers: the nurse reads a value and the patient or relative disagrees or remembers another (a dose, a weight, a BP). Keep both and record an uncertainty.

stopped_or_never_taken: a medicine the patient stopped, was never given or only took once ('I stopped it in March'). Status discontinued, not current; a medicine never taken is not recorded as a medication.

omissions.text: Current amlodipine dose is reported by patient/husband as 5 mg (little white tablet; box says 5 mg), not just unspecified amlodipine every other day.
Nurse reported the file/script says amlodipine 10 mg once daily.
Aspirin was mentioned after a hospital visit but the patient never started it, not even once.
Negative finding asked and answered: no headaches was initially stated before the patient clarified she does get a small headache now and then behind the eyes.
Alcohol use detail: only a glass of wine at a braai / one glass at the Saturday braai.
Examination/vitals detail: pulse was regular at 72.
Doctor said the patient looks well.
Fasting instruction detail: blood tests to be done tomorrow morning before any coffee.
Plan detail: statin decision deferred until results reviewed together in a month; doctor explicitly said he would not pressure/scold her and if cholesterol is fine the statin stays off.
Patient expressed reluctance to restart statin: 'I'm not promising I'll start it again.'
